section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the 23-item Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2; Tylka & Van Diest, 2013) and notes that the validated Portuguese version (Duarte, Pinto Gouveia, & Mendes, 2016) was used in Portugal. It outlines the 5-point response scale, the four IES-2 dimensions, and states that total and subscale scores were used; it also reports prior reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .85–.89) and 3-week stability (r = .88–.92) in college samples. The section notes no study has investigated IES-2 psychometrics among adolescents but cites Dockendorff et al. (2012) regarding the original IES in young adolescents. No mention of 'Study 1' or multiple sample subsets appears.
section_summary.evidence_source: Sentences used: "The 23-item Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2; Tylka & Van Diest, 2013) was used to assess intuitive eating." "The already validated Portuguese version (Duarte, Pinto Gouveia, & Mendes, 2016) was used in Portugal." "Items are rated on a 5-point scale ranging from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)." "The IES-2 is composed of four dimensions... The total scale and subscale scores were used in the present study." "The total IES-2 scores have evidenced good internal reliability (Cronbach  = .85–.89) and 3-week stability (r = .88–.92) in samples of college women and men (Tylka & Van Diest, 2013)." "Although no study has investigated the psychometric properties of the IES-2 among adolescents, Dockendorff, Petrie, Greenleaf, and Martin (2012) reported that the original IES could be used among young adolescents."
